item.title: Blue Wahoos Fall to Biscuits, Playoff Hopes Remain Uncertain

The loss keeps the Wahoos from shrinking their magic number, leaving their postseason hopes hanging in the balance heading into the final stretch of the season. The team managed just two runs…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos' bid to clinch a playoff berth fell short Sunday as they dropped a 7-2 decision to the Montgomery Biscuits in the series finale.

The loss keeps the Wahoos from shrinking their magic number, leaving their postseason hopes hanging in the balance heading into the final stretch of the season. The team managed just two runs against the Biscuits' lineup, unable to mount the offensive push needed to secure the playoff spot.

The Blue Wahoos will look to bounce back as they continue their push toward clinching a playoff position in the coming days.

item.title: Typical summer heat returns to Pensacola area this week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: North Escambia can expect temperatures climbing into the low 90s this week, with the best chances for rain hitting midweek, according to the National Weather Service forecast. Monday will start mostly sunny with highs near 91 degrees and just a 30 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms after 1 p.m. Northeast winds around 5 mph will shift to…
item.content:encoded:
North Escambia can expect temperatures climbing into the low 90s this week, with the best chances for rain hitting midweek, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

Monday will start mostly sunny with highs near 91 degrees and just a 30 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms after 1 p.m. Northeast winds around 5 mph will shift to the southeast during the afternoon. Monday night should cool to around 73 degrees with partly cloudy skies and a 20 percent chance of isolated showers before 10 p.m.

Forecasters say rain chances will peak by Wednesday and Thursday as moisture increases, so residents should keep an eye on the forecast if they have outdoor plans mid-week. The typical summer pattern of afternoon heat and scattered storms looks to continue through the period.

item.title: Gas Prices Edge Up To $3.89 As Labor Day Weekend Approaches
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida drivers heading into the Labor Day weekend will find slightly higher prices at the pump, with the state average for regular unleaded hitting $3.89 per gallon this week. That's a 3-cent jump from the previous week, according to AAA. While the uptick is modest, it continues a pattern that's held steady throughout the summer months. For…
item.content:encoded:
Florida drivers heading into the Labor Day weekend will find slightly higher prices at the pump, with the state average for regular unleaded hitting $3.89 per gallon this week. That's a 3-cent jump from the previous week, according to AAA.

While the uptick is modest, it continues a pattern that's held steady throughout the summer months. For Pensacola-area drivers planning holiday trips over the long weekend, the price hike is unlikely to dramatically change travel plans, but it's worth factoring into fuel budgets for extended drives to the beach or out of state.

AAA notes that despite weekly fluctuations, gas prices have remained relatively stable compared to price swings seen in previous years. Motorists looking to stretch their fuel dollars might consider filling up earlier in the week rather than waiting until the weekend when demand typically pushes prices higher.

item.title: Century Teen Charged in Fatal Showalter Park Shooting Moved to Adult Court

Keyunta Iveon Ewing, who goes by the nickname "Baby K," appeared before a judge Friday for the transfer hearing. He faces a first-degree murder charge stemming from…
item.content:encoded:
A 16-year-old Century resident has been transferred to adult court and is being held without bond in connection with a fatal shooting at Showalter Park, according to court documents.

Keyunta Iveon Ewing, who goes by the nickname "Baby K," appeared before a judge Friday for the transfer hearing. He faces a first-degree murder charge stemming from the incident at the park.

The teen's case was moved from juvenile court to the adult system following the hearing. Ewing remains in custody without the possibility of bail as the case proceeds through the criminal justice system.

Details about the circumstances of the shooting and Ewing's defense claims were not immediately available. The case is ongoing.

item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment resident faces felony charges after authorities say he stole commercial light fixtures from an active downtown Pensacola construction site. Joseph Wade Walling, 52, of Twilight Drive, was arrested and charged with grand theft from a posted construction site, according to court records.

Walling entered a not guilty plea to the charge. The alleged theft occurred at a construction site in downtown Pensacola, where the fixtures were taken from a secured work area.

The case remains pending in Escambia County courts. Grand theft charges in Florida can carry significant penalties depending on the value of items taken and prior criminal history.

item.title: Florida Cattle Ranchers Blast Trump's Beef Import Plan
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's cattle ranching community is pushing back against President Donald Trump's announcement of a tariff-free beef import deal aimed at lowering consumer prices. Trump said the arrangement would bring in 300,000 tons of imported beef and reduce prices by as much as 25 percent, according to social media posts from the president. The plan has…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's cattle ranching community is pushing back against President Donald Trump's announcement of a tariff-free beef import deal aimed at lowering consumer prices. Trump said the arrangement would bring in 300,000 tons of imported beef and reduce prices by as much as 25 percent, according to social media posts from the president.

The plan has drawn criticism from local ranchers who argue the influx of foreign beef could undercut their own operations and livelihoods. While Trump blamed inflationary pressures from the Biden administration for the need to lower beef costs, ranchers contend that opening the market to massive imports isn't the answer.

The disagreement highlights a broader tension in agricultural policy: balancing consumer demand for affordable food with support for domestic farming and ranching operations. For Northwest Florida's cattle industry, the outcome of this policy dispute could have real economic consequences.

item.title: Two Escambia County Fentanyl Dealers Get 5 Years Each in Federal Prison
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Two Escambia County residents have been sentenced to five years in federal prison on fentanyl trafficking charges, according to court records. Thomas Christopher Morton, 47, and Laurie Ann Chapman, 54, each received the same sentence after convictions related to distributing the powerful opioid. Federal prosecutors say the case is part of an…
item.content:encoded:
Two Escambia County residents have been sentenced to five years in federal prison on fentanyl trafficking charges, according to court records.

Thomas Christopher Morton, 47, and Laurie Ann Chapman, 54, each received the same sentence after convictions related to distributing the powerful opioid. Federal prosecutors say the case is part of an ongoing crackdown on fentanyl trafficking throughout the region.

Fentanyl has become one of the most significant drug threats facing law enforcement in Northwest Florida and across the country. The synthetic opioid is often mixed into other drugs without users' knowledge, making it particularly deadly.

The sentencing reflects federal judges' commitment to prosecuting major drug trafficking operations, though both local and federal agencies continue to report rising fentanyl seizures across Escambia County.

item.title: FDOT Weighing Two Safety Options for Highway 29 and Highway 196 Intersection
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation is evaluating how to improve safety at the busy intersection of Highway 29 and Highway 196 (Barrineau Park Road) in North Escambia County, considering two distinctly different approaches. The first option involves installing a traditional traffic signal at the location. The second alternative is an RCUT…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation is evaluating how to improve safety at the busy intersection of Highway 29 and Highway 196 (Barrineau Park Road) in North Escambia County, considering two distinctly different approaches.

The first option involves installing a traditional traffic signal at the location. The second alternative is an RCUT intersection—short for Restricted Crossing U-Turn—which would redesign the intersection to require vehicles to make U-turns on Highway 29 in order to cross over, rather than turning directly across the highway.

RCUT intersections have become increasingly common in transportation planning across Florida and the nation as a way to improve safety and traffic flow at high-speed corridors. The restricted design eliminates certain turning conflicts that can lead to accidents.

FDOT has not yet announced which option it will pursue or a timeline for construction. Residents and commuters in the North Escambia area who use that corridor regularly are encouraged to monitor FDOT announcements for additional details about the project.

item.content:encoded:
A boil water notice is now in effect for residents in the Gonzalez area following a broken water main, according to North Escambia reports.

The notice applies to customers in two specific zones: addresses 1797-2181 on Pauline Street and 792-798 on Rusty Lane. The precautionary measure was implemented after a 4-inch water main serving the area broke, potentially compromising water quality in the affected sections.

Residents under the notice are advised to boil water before using it for drinking, cooking, or ice-making until further notice. Affected customers should monitor local water authority updates for notification when the boil water order is lifted.

item.title: Major I-10 crash near Alabama-Mississippi line closes westbound lanes for hours
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A significant crash shut down westbound Interstate 10 near the Alabama-Mississippi state line early Sunday morning, backing up traffic for miles and forcing emergency crews from multiple agencies to work several hours to clear the roadway. The collision occurred before 6 a.m. near mile marker 2 in Mobile County, Alabama, according to WKRG News 5.…
item.content:encoded:
A significant crash shut down westbound Interstate 10 near the Alabama-Mississippi state line early Sunday morning, backing up traffic for miles and forcing emergency crews from multiple agencies to work several hours to clear the roadway.

The collision occurred before 6 a.m. near mile marker 2 in Mobile County, Alabama, according to WKRG News 5. Westbound traffic was completely closed for approximately four hours while emergency responders worked to clear debris and assess any injuries.

While the incident occurred west of the Pensacola market, major crashes along the I-10 corridor can impact regional travel patterns, particularly for drivers heading west toward Louisiana or those returning to Northwest Florida from Alabama.

No additional details about the cause of the crash or the number of vehicles involved were immediately available. Drivers planning to travel on I-10 westbound should anticipate possible residual delays as traffic flow normalizes.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos kept their winning streak alive Saturday night with a 5-2 victory over the Montgomery Biscuits, moving within striking distance of the South Division second half championship.

The win marked the Blue Wahoos' third straight triumph and reduced their magic number to six games as they pursue the divisional title. The team's momentum heading into the final stretch of the season suggests they're hitting their stride at a critical time.

According to reporting from North Escambia, the Blue Wahoos set a home run record in the victory, though specifics on that mark weren't immediately detailed. The offensive outburst proved the difference against the Biscuits in what was a solid all-around performance for the Pensacola squad.

item.title: Florida Weighs AI Rules for College Students, Vaccine Requirements
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As students settle into the new school year, Florida education officials are grappling with how to regulate artificial intelligence use on college campuses, while state health authorities are pushing to reduce the number of vaccines required for school attendance. The dual policy discussions reflect broader debates playing out across Florida's…
item.content:encoded:
As students settle into the new school year, Florida education officials are grappling with how to regulate artificial intelligence use on college campuses, while state health authorities are pushing to reduce the number of vaccines required for school attendance.

The dual policy discussions reflect broader debates playing out across Florida's education system. College administrators and educators say they need clear guidelines on when and how students can use AI tools in coursework, as the technology becomes increasingly prevalent in academic settings.

Meanwhile, health officials have suggested loosening vaccine requirements currently mandated for students to enroll in schools. The proposal has drawn attention as states nationwide reconsider immunization policies in the post-pandemic era.

Both issues are expected to see further discussion as the Florida Legislature prepares for upcoming sessions and education boards consider regulatory changes.

item.title: FWC Offers Free Hunter Safety Courses Across North Escambia in September
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is hosting free hunter safety courses throughout North Escambia County this month, with classroom sessions scheduled in Molino, Cantonment, Jay, and Milton. The courses are designed to teach students proper hunting safety practices, conservation principles, and responsible hunting habits.…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is hosting free hunter safety courses throughout North Escambia County this month, with classroom sessions scheduled in Molino, Cantonment, Jay, and Milton.

The courses are designed to teach students proper hunting safety practices, conservation principles, and responsible hunting habits. Participants can complete the online portion of the course at their own pace before attending an in-person class session in their area.

According to the FWC, hunter safety certification is required for anyone born after June 1, 1975 who wants to hunt in Florida. The courses cover firearm safety, hunting regulations, wildlife management, and ethical hunting practices.

Interested hunters can register online at the FWC website and choose their preferred class location. More details about specific dates and times for the North Escambia sessions are available through the FWC's hunter safety program page.

item.content:encoded:
Drivers heading through Escambia County should expect slowdowns on Interstate 10 as resurfacing work continues east of U.S. 231, according to a weekly traffic report from the Florida Department of Transportation.

The ongoing construction project is part of routine maintenance to keep the major corridor in working condition. Crews are actively working on the roadway, which means motorists should anticipate reduced speeds and possible lane closures during daylight hours.

Travelers are urged to allow extra time for their commutes and remain alert in work zones. Alternative routes may be available depending on your destination, so checking real-time traffic conditions before heading out is recommended.

For the most up-to-date information on construction timelines and potential delays, drivers can check the FDOT website or local traffic reports.

item.content:encoded:
An inmate at Century Correctional Institution has been convicted and sentenced to additional prison time after authorities discovered a substantial amount of methamphetamine and other contraband during a routine search.

The discovery highlighted ongoing challenges with drug trafficking within correctional facilities in Escambia County. The inmate was found with what investigators determined was a trafficking quantity of methamphetamine, leading to additional charges beyond his original sentence.

Century Correctional Institution, located in North Escambia County, continues to work with law enforcement to prevent contraband from entering the facility and to maintain security within the prison. The case underscores the persistent problem of drug smuggling in Florida's corrections system, where inmates and outside collaborators frequently attempt to bring controlled substances into facilities.

Residents heading out early in the day should have clear conditions, but those planning afternoon activities may want to keep an eye on developing storm chances. The heat and humidity will remain typical for this time of year across the Escambia and Santa Rosa County areas.

item.title: Frontier Ending Copper Landline Service Across North Escambia Communities
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Frontier Communications is phasing out traditional copper-based landline phone service in several Northwest Florida communities, including Walnut Hill, Molino, and Bratt, as well as parts of Alabama near Atmore. The telecommunications company has already secured FCC approval for the service discontinuation in Alabama. A similar application to…
item.content:encoded:
Frontier Communications is phasing out traditional copper-based landline phone service in several Northwest Florida communities, including Walnut Hill, Molino, and Bratt, as well as parts of Alabama near Atmore.

The telecommunications company has already secured FCC approval for the service discontinuation in Alabama. A similar application to retire legacy telephone infrastructure in Frontier's Florida service area is moving through the federal approval process.

Residents and businesses still relying on Frontier's copper landlines in these areas will need to transition to alternative phone services. Frontier has been gradually shifting customers toward fiber-optic and digital alternatives as part of a broader industry trend away from aging copper infrastructure. Customers affected by the change should contact Frontier directly to explore available service options in their area.

item.title: Mobile's Crafts and Drafts Market Connects Local Vendors With Shoppers
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A monthly market in downtown Mobile is creating opportunities for small business owners to connect directly with customers while giving shoppers a chance to support local vendors. Crafts and Drafts returned to Oyster City Brewing Company on Saturday evening, according to WKRG News 5, drawing crowds from 5 to 9 p.m. The recurring event has become a…
item.content:encoded: A monthly market in downtown Mobile is creating opportunities for small business owners to connect directly with customers while giving shoppers a chance to support local vendors. Crafts and Drafts returned to Oyster City Brewing Company on Saturday evening, according to WKRG News 5, drawing crowds from 5 to 9 p.m. The recurring event has become a popular gathering spot in the area, combining the appeal of handmade goods with the casual atmosphere of a local brewery. For small business owners in the Mobile area, the market provides a lower-cost way to test products, build brand awareness, and establish relationships with repeat customers without the overhead of a permanent retail location. The event also gives shoppers an alternative to chain retailers, offering unique, locally-made items while supporting entrepreneurs in their community.

Residents in the affected area were advised to monitor local updates from the Prichard Public Services Department for information on restoration efforts and any boil-water notices.

item.title: MoonPie Over Mobile to announce 2027 headliners soon
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The MoonPie Over Mobile New Year celebration is building anticipation with a countdown timer to reveal the main musical acts that will headline the popular Gulf Coast event as revelers prepare to ring in 2027. The annual celebration, held in Mobile, Alabama, draws thousands of visitors to downtown for its iconic MoonPie drop and live…
item.content:encoded:
The MoonPie Over Mobile New Year celebration is building anticipation with a countdown timer to reveal the main musical acts that will headline the popular Gulf Coast event as revelers prepare to ring in 2027.

The annual celebration, held in Mobile, Alabama, draws thousands of visitors to downtown for its iconic MoonPie drop and live entertainment. Organizers have made a practice of keeping headliner announcements suspenseful, releasing performers in stages leading up to the final event.

While specific dates and performer names haven't yet been released, fans of the celebration can expect details to roll out in the coming weeks as the countdown progresses. The event remains one of the region's largest New Year's Eve gatherings.
